h1: Hotel Holm Bangkok — New 3-Star Residence with Spacious Rooms on Ratchawithi 2, Steps from Bangkok's Hospital District
intro: When you need a quiet, comfortable base near Bangkok's densest cluster of public hospitals — or simply want more room than the price usually buys — Hotel Holm Bangkok delivers on both counts. This brand-new boutique residence on Soi Ratchawithi 2 in Phaya Thai opened in 2025 with apartment-style rooms featuring fridges and Netflix, free parking for self-driving guests, and a complimentary shuttle to BTS Victory Monument. Rajavithi Hospital is a roughly 650m walk away (about 8 minutes), and Queen Sirikit National Institute of Child Health follows along the same road. Starting from approx. ฿1,174/night, with a score of 9.3 from 136 verified reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: Hotel Holm Bangkok — known before rebranding as VDA Residence — opened in 2025 on Soi Ratchawithi 2, a quiet residential lane branching off Ratchawithi Road in Phaya Thai. The location sits squarely in Bangkok's medical corridor: Rajavithi Hospital lies about 650m away (an 8-minute walk), and the Queen Sirikit National Institute of Child Health — one of Thailand's leading children's hospitals — is another few hundred metres further along the same road. For families who have come to Bangkok to accompany a patient through treatment, this proximity is the single biggest reason to choose the hotel.

The rooms are consistently the most praised aspect in guest feedback. The Exclusive Corner Holm measures 31sqm — genuinely spacious for a three-star hotel in Bangkok — with windows on two sides, a King bed, blackout curtains, in-room fridge, electric kettle, a flat-screen TV with Netflix, and a private bathroom with a proper rain shower. Standard Double Holm and Twin Holm rooms are smaller but still comfortable, and most come with a window and the same amenities. The consensus from long-stay guests is that the rooms feel more like a serviced apartment than a city hotel.
"Very spacious rooms, spotlessly clean. The staff arranged our shuttle to BTS every morning without us having to ask twice. Five nights here and we'd stay again."

Breakfast is served at Hart Breakfast, the in-house restaurant, running 06:30–11:00 daily as an American-and-Thai buffet with fresh fruit, congee, eggs, and a decent coffee machine. Breakfast is not included in the standard room rate — it costs an additional ฿190 per adult, which is reasonable value compared to local street prices. Adding it at the time of booking usually works out cheaper than paying at the door. The free on-site parking is another major draw: self-driving visitors from upcountry frequently cite it as the deciding factor in choosing the hotel over competitors.

The hotel runs a complimentary shuttle to BTS Victory Monument station, which is otherwise a roughly 950-metre walk. Request the shuttle the night before or at the front desk in the morning — it is not a continuous service but a scheduled run, and staff are generally responsive. Local bus routes along Ratchawithi Road are a practical alternative for short hops within the neighbourhood, and Grab taxis can be called from the soi, though the narrow lane can sometimes slow pick-up access during rush hour.

Soi Ratchawithi 2 is a residential side street. There is no convenience store at the hotel entrance, and the nearest 7-Eleven requires a few minutes' walk. For guests whose primary purpose is hospital visits, this tradeoff is minor — the quiet surroundings make for better rest after a stressful day. For travellers looking to explore shops, markets, or nightlife, the neighbourhood is functional rather than exciting.

The Trip.com score of 9.3 from 136 reviews breaks down into cleanliness at 9.5, facilities at 9.4, service at 9.4, and location at 9.0 — a pattern that reflects a well-run, freshly opened property. A small number of guests reported minor plumbing issues, AC inconsistencies, and one instance of ants on a bathroom vanity. In each documented case, front desk staff responded quickly when notified. Teething problems in a first-year property are not unusual, and the overall trajectory of reviews is strongly positive.

Honestly: Hotel Holm Bangkok is the best fit for multi-night stays near Rajavithi Hospital or Queen Sirikit National Institute of Child Health, for guests driving in from the provinces, or anyone who wants genuinely spacious rooms at a budget-friendly price. It is not the right choice if you need to be within a minute's walk of the BTS, or if you want a rooftop pool, restaurant scene, or vibrant neighbourhood to explore. Within its defined purpose, though, it performs at a level well above its category.

honestSummary: Hotel Holm Bangkok earns its high score from guests who need exactly what it offers: spacious, clean rooms in a quiet lane within easy reach of Rajavithi Hospital and the Children's Hospital, with free parking and a free BTS shuttle. It falls short only if you need the BTS on your doorstep or a full-service hotel environment.
honestChecks: If you need to be directly beside the BTS or in a lively shopping district — Soi Ratchawithi 2 is not that place; the free shuttle helps but adds a scheduling step → consider hotels closer to the BTS Victory Monument interchange

If you encounter a room issue at check-in (plumbing, AC, insects) — report it to the front desk immediately; the hotel's track record shows quick resolution, and it is always better to flag it early than endure the problem

If you are travelling with family and want breakfast included — add the breakfast package at booking (฿190 per adult); it works out cheaper than buying at the door and the buffet quality is genuinely above budget-hotel average

tips.title: Self-Drive Guests: Free Parking
tips.body: On-site parking is free of charge — exceptionally rare in this part of Bangkok. Mention at booking and confirm with the hotel the day before to ensure a space is reserved.

tips.title: Book the BTS Shuttle in Advance
tips.body: The free shuttle to BTS Victory Monument runs on request, not continuously. Tell the front desk the evening before what time you need it — this avoids any wait in the morning.

tips.title: Walking Route to Rajavithi Hospital
tips.body: Exit the soi, turn left onto Ratchawithi Road and walk approximately 650m — roughly 8 minutes at a comfortable pace. The main hospital entrance faces the road. Queen Sirikit Children's Hospital is a few hundred metres further on the same side.

tips.title: Add Breakfast When Booking
tips.body: Breakfast (Hart Breakfast buffet, 06:30–11:00) is not included in the standard rate but costs only ฿190 per adult. Adding it at the time of online booking is usually cheaper than paying at the restaurant.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Hotel Holm Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Hotel Holm Bangkok and which hospitals are nearby?
faq.a: Hotel Holm Bangkok is at 10 Soi Ratchawithi 2, Samsen Nai, Phaya Thai, Bangkok 10400. Rajavithi Hospital is roughly 650m away (about 8 minutes on foot), and Queen Sirikit National Institute of Child Health is about 800m along the same road. BTS Victory Monument is approximately 950m away, with a free hotel shuttle available.

faq.q: What are the room types and prices at Hotel Holm Bangkok?
faq.a: Rooms start from approx. ฿1,174/night for the Double Holm (King bed, window, fridge, Netflix). Twin Holm with two single beds starts around ฿1,250. The Exclusive Corner Holm (31sqm, floors 5–8, King bed with corner window view) starts around ฿1,500. Prices vary by date and booking platform.

faq.q: Does Hotel Holm Bangkok have free parking?
faq.a: Yes — on-site parking is free of charge for hotel guests. This is a significant advantage in this part of Bangkok where parking is scarce. Inform the hotel at the time of booking or call ahead to confirm availability for your arrival.

faq.q: How do I get to BTS Victory Monument from Hotel Holm Bangkok?
faq.a: The hotel offers a complimentary shuttle service to BTS Victory Monument on request. It is not a continuous service, so arrange the timing with the front desk the evening before. Alternatively, the station is about a 950m walk or a short Grab ride.

faq.q: Is Hotel Holm Bangkok good for a long multi-night stay?
faq.a: Yes — it is well-suited for multi-night stays. Spacious apartment-style rooms with a fridge and Netflix, free parking, daily buffet breakfast option, and a quiet residential setting all support comfortable extended stays. It is particularly popular with families accompanying patients at nearby hospitals.
